title: Round 767 (F1073): claim-system CORRECTION via exhaustive writer scan + real-data measurement - F1072's 'dynamic entity claim' interpretation REVISED to a STATIC-ID HIGHLIGHT system: (1) exhaustive .text writer scans for cell byte9 (all addressing forms: mod01 reg-direct 88/80, SIB 44/4C/54/5C/64/6C/74/7C, word-imm at +8) find ZERO byte9 writers - the only hits are the effect-record init 0x437B1A (mov word[edi+8],0xDC - the F1070 0x20B record, not a map cell) and unaligned false positives; no or/and-0x80/0x7F forms exist at all; (2) real-data measurement over 60 valid 14B-cell maps (3,352,976 cells): byte9 bit7 set on only 282 cells (0.008%); byte9 & 0x7F nonzero on ~10,156 cells with clustered values {11:2761, 10:2227, 9:2047, 60:968, 1:889, 58:851, 61:194} - a sparse static per-cell id field (door/trigger/object ids [INFERENCE]); byte11 bit7 NEVER set in any file (0/3.35M) = pure runtime mark, consistent with 0x43C1B0 set / 0x43C270 clear; byte10 in {0, 4} only (0x04 on 9,971 cells) = static flag byte; (3) REVISED SEMANTICS: 0x43C1B0(x,y,id) marks all cells in the 18x18 window whose STATIC byte9-id equals the argument id (e.g. highlight every cell belonging to object/door id N), 0x43C270 unmarks them, 0x43C150 'free-or-marked' gate + 0x43C0F0 id read feed the hero approach-step scan against these static ids - so the F1072 step engine walks toward cells tagged with a given static id (door/trigger approach), not toward dynamically-claimed entity cells; (4) net cell-record state after F1065/F1069/F1072/F1073: bytes 0-9 + 11 + word 0xC anchored; byte10 = static flag (0x04); bytes 12-13 (high word of attr dword) still unmapped
objective: Find the occupancy writers and measure the claim bytes on real data.
question: Who writes byte9, and what do bytes 9-11 contain in real map files?
method: Exhaustive instruction-pattern scan (direct/SIB/word-imm forms) over .text; byte9/10/11 histogram over 3.35M cells from 60 valid maps.

cell_analysis.byte9: static id (99.7% zero; cluster {9,10,11,58,60,61,1}); bit7 rare (282/3.35M)
cell_analysis.byte11_bit7: never set in files - runtime mark only (0x43C1B0/0x43C270 pair)
cell_analysis.writers: none in .text (0x437B1A = effect record, not cell)
cell_analysis.mark_unmark: 0x43C1B0 / 0x43C270 keyed by static byte9-id match in 18x18 window

audit_vs_exe.F1072: CORRECTED: 'occupant id' is a static map-data id; no runtime claim writers exist; approach-step targets static-id-marked cells
audit_vs_exe.F1069: byte10 now anchored (static flag 0x04); remaining unmapped: bytes 12-13
audit_vs_exe.F1070: 0x437B1A correctly attributed to the effect record (mov word[edi+8],0xDC)

verdict: The occupancy/claim layer is a static-id highlight system: map data carries sparse per-cell ids, runtime code marks/unmarks matching cells in an 18x18 window, and the hero approach scan walks toward marked cells.
evidence_level_note: Absence-of-writers proof via exhaustive pattern scan; byte semantics from 3.35M-cell measurement on original client data.
reproduce: scan 88/80 mod01+SIB disp8=9 and 66 C7 +8 over .text; histogram buf[i+9..i+11] over Map/*.map
notes: byte9-id cluster {9,10,11,58,60,61} suggests grouped object/trigger ids
